title: Elevator Controller Simulation

visible.label: Sweeps upward serving all upper stops before reversing downward
visible.script:
e = Elevator(1, 10, 4)
e.request(5)
e.request(2)
e.request(7)
assert e.run_until_idle() == [5, 6, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2]
assert e.status() == {"floor": 2, "direction": 0, "pending": []}

visible.label: Tie-breaks equidistant requests upward from idle
visible.inputDisplay: start=5; req 3 and 7 -> goes up to 7 first
visible.script:
e = Elevator(1, 10, 5)
e.request(3)
e.request(7)
assert e.run_until_idle() == [6, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3]

hidden.label: Out-of-range constructor or request raises ValueError
Request at current idle floor is immediately satisfied without extra step
hidden.script:
e = Elevator(1, 10, 4)
e.request(4)
assert e.run_until_idle() == []
assert e.status() == {"floor": 4, "direction": 0, "pending": []}

hidden.label: Mid-sweep dynamically added request above gets picked up on same pass
hidden.inputDisplay: start=1, req(4), step x2 (now floor 3), req(2) & req(5)
hidden.script:
e = Elevator(1, 10, 1)
e.request(4)
assert e.step() == 2
assert e.step() == 3
e.request(2)
e.request(5)
assert e.run_until_idle() == [4, 5, 4, 3, 2]

hidden.label: Duplicate floor requests are deduplicated
hidden.script:
e = Elevator(1, 10, 2)
e.request(4)
e.request(4)
assert e.status()["pending"] == [4]

hidden.label: Downward sweep first when closer stop is below
hidden.inputDisplay: start=6; req 5 and 9 -> down to 5 then up to 9
hidden.script:
e = Elevator(1, 10, 6)
e.request(5)
e.request(9)
assert e.run_until_idle() == [5, 6, 7, 8, 9]

hints: Use the directional SCAN/LOOK policy: keep moving in the current direction (`+1` or `-1`) as long as any pending stop exists in that direction!
Only when moving `up` and NO pending stops `> floor` remain, reverse to `-1` (if pending `< floor` exists) or go idle (`0`). Mirror for `down`.

If idle (`direction == 0`) with non-empty pending stops: choose the nearest floor `target = min(pending, key=lambda f: (abs(f - floor), -f))` so upward ties beat downward ties (`-f` is smaller when `f > floor`).
